clue.text: Mundane arguments for backing organization of agents

parts.note: the pros are the arguments in favour, as in pros and cons

indicators.note: something backing runs in the opposite direction, so the agents' organization is read from its end

parts.note: the Central Intelligence Agency, the US spy organization

explanation.surface: Someone finds the case for reshuffling a spy agency tedious and uninspired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organization' looks like an anagram signal, but here it is the literal noun: the agency itself, the CIA, turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosaic writing or thinking is dull and ordinary, lacking any poetry, which is exactly what mundane describes.

clue.text: One likely to succeed, when finally put in charge

indicators.note: put in says the tail of 'when' is placed inside the word for charge

parts.note: a charge is the price asked for something

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word before it, 'when'

parts.note: the last letter of 'when'

explanation.surface: A promising young candidate is tipped to make it once they're finally given responsibility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One likely to succeed' reads as a high-flyer; in fact 'succeed' means inherit a throne, as a prince will succeed the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A prince, as heir, is expected to follow the reigning king or queen on the throne.

clue.text: Size of book, a volume penned by doctor, extremely abridged

indicators.note: abridged at the extremes means the doctor loses both first and last letters
what is penned by something is written inside it, so the article and volume sit within the shortened doctor

parts.note: DOCTOR without its outer D and R
the article as it stands
V is the standard abbreviation for volume

explanation.surface: A bibliographer notes a book's format while a doctor has written a heavily cut-down volume.
explanation.walkthrough: The doctor here is the whole word DOCTOR, trimmed at each end, not an abbreviation like DR or MO.
explanation.definitionFit: Octavo is a traditional book format, made by folding printed sheets into eight leaves, so it names a page size.

clue.text: Medical practitioner needs to go to France with substance

parts.note: aller is the French verb meaning to go
the gist of something is its substance or main point

explanation.surface: A doctor has to travel to France, taking some medicine along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To go to France' means 'to go' in France, i.e. rendered in French; 'with' simply joins the second piece on.
explanation.definitionFit: An allergist is a physician specialising in allergies and immune reactions, a kind of medical specialist.

clue.text: Measure of coolness about female player securing prominence

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so the leading abbreviation and the female player hold the prominence between them

parts.note: c. is short for circa, Latin for about
a hill is a prominence in the landscape
F is the standard abbreviation for female
a player on stage is an actor

explanation.surface: A casting agent sizes up how cool a leading actress is, as she wins star billing.
explanation.walkthrough: Wind chill is the weather sense: 'coolness' is literal cold, not the calm or style the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: The chill factor is the weather reading of how cold it feels once wind is taken into account.

clue.text: More than one error in small volume is infuriating

parts.note: cl is a centilitre, a small measure of volume
something that is infuriating angers you

explanation.surface: Finding several mistakes packed into one slim book is maddening.
explanation.walkthrough: A clanger is British slang for a blunder, especially an embarrassing one; the plural is needed for 'more than one'. 'Small volume' is a measure of liquid, not a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Clangers are glaring mistakes or gaffes, colloquially, so the plural matches several errors.

clue.text: Rubbed it in hands

definitions.meaning: gloated: an old past tense of the verb crow, meaning boast
hands are workers, as on a ship: all hands on deck

explanation.surface: Someone massaged a cream into their palms.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is massage; the first sense is gloating, and the answer is an old past tense of crow (as in 'before the cock crew'), besides being the noun for workers.
explanation.definitionFit: To crow is to boast over someone, so the archaic past tense means gloated; a ship's hands form its workforce.

clue.text: Presenters with a warning about food king's tucked into

indicators.note: about means around, so the warning with its article wraps round everything that follows
the king's letter is tucked into the food, sitting inside it

parts.note: the article as it stands
'n' is the short form of and, as in rock 'n' roll, so it stands for with
chow is slang for food
R is Rex, Latin for king
an omen is a warning sign of what is to come

explanation.surface: TV presenters give a warning about some food the king has been eating greedily.
explanation.walkthrough: The outer layer is 'a warning' split round the rest; inside, the king's R sits within CHOW, with the N from 'with' placed ahead of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Anchorwomen are the lead female presenters of news programmes, who front and link the broadcast.

clue.text: With leader in Guardian, say, crush inferior competition

indicators.note: the leader in a word is its first letter, here of 'Guardian'

parts.note: the opening letter of Guardian
to say something is to utter it
to crush grapes is to press them

explanation.surface: A newspaper wants to flatten its downmarket rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guardian, say' looks like a definition by example, but 'say' is UTTER and the definition is at the far end: tabloids are the Guardian's inferior competition.
explanation.definitionFit: The gutter press is the sensationalist tabloid newspapers, seen by a quality broadsheet as lowbrow rivals.

clue.text: Reviving spiritual instruction's pressing

parts.note: RE is religious education, a British school subject
the possessive S taken as a letter
a pressing matter is an urgent one

explanation.surface: Religious teaching is in urgent need of a revival.
explanation.walkthrough: RE, religious education, is the name for the school subject in British schools.
explanation.definitionFit: Something resurgent is rising again after a decline, coming back to life and strength.

clue.text: Penny taken in by French writer's university position

indicators.note: what is taken in by something ends up inside it, so the coin letter goes inside the author's name

parts.note: Albert Camus, the French novelist of The Outsider
p is short for penny

explanation.surface: A French author fell for a woman called Penny and so landed an academic post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'University position' reads as a job, but it is a physical location: where a university stands.
explanation.definitionFit: A campus is the grounds and buildings of a university, its physical site or location.

clue.text: Ran in and stopped

definitions.meaning: police slang for taking someone into custody
halted, as a disease's progress may be

explanation.surface: Someone dashed indoors and then stood still.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ran in' is informal British for having a suspect taken to the police station, not running indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Police who run someone in detain them; separately, to check or halt progress is the same verb's other sense.

clue.text: Mixing up of insecticides is not empirically based

indicators.note: mixing jumbles the letters of 'up of insecticides' together

parts.note: anagram fodder, sixteen letters

explanation.surface: Blending pesticides together, it is said, has no proper evidence behind it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixing up' looks like one phrase, but only 'Mixing' signals; 'up' is two letters of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pseudoscientific claims scientific status without resting on observation or tested evidence.

clue.text: Attachment to vehicle that's sped and is overturned

indicators.note: in a down clue, overturned turns the column upside down, so the words for sped and 'and is' read upwards

parts.note: to speed is to race
'is' as it stands, added on

explanation.surface: A trailer on a speeding car has flipped over.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a road accident; 'overturned' is really the instruction to read the two pieces backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidecar is the one-wheeled passenger car fixed to the side of a motorcycle.

clue.text: As result of performance on this, I queue in audition?

definitions.text: As result of performance on this
definitions.note: the exam whose result is the score the wordplay spells

indicators.note: in audition means as heard, so 'I queue' is taken by its sound

parts.note: said aloud, the two words are the letters of the intelligence quotient

explanation.surface: A hopeful performer ends up standing in line at an audition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I queue' spoken aloud is IQ, the intelligence quotient; the whole clue then describes the exam that produces that score.
explanation.definitionFit: An IQ figure is the score produced by sitting this standardised mental-ability exam.

clue.text: Demon capturing rook, leading to mate

indicators.note: the demon captures the chess piece, holding it inside

parts.note: a fiend is a demon
R is the chess notation for rook

explanation.surface: A fiendish chess player takes a rook on the way to checkmate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rook' and 'mate' both look like chess; 'mate' is really a pal.
explanation.definitionFit: Mate is informal British and Australian usage for a pal, a companion or buddy.

clue.text: Our confidant reveals end of scandal over job

parts.note: -gate is the suffix tacked onto scandals since Watergate
a post is a job; 'over' places the scandal piece above it in a down clue

explanation.surface: A trusted insider leaks the final twist of a scandal about somebody's job.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'between you and me and the gatepost' marks a secret; the post is the third party, our confidant. 'End of scandal' is the -gate suffix, not a final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In the saying for sharing secrets, the gatepost is the silent third party sworn to discretion.

clue.text: Caught out in the open? Just the opposite

definitions.note: means the reverse of 'in the open'

parts.note: c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
doing something openly, out in the open, is doing it overtly

explanation.surface: Someone is caught out in public view, or rather quite the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay builds 'caught, out in the open' literally, then 'Just the opposite' supplies the definition: the answer means the reverse of openly.
explanation.definitionFit: Covert action is secret and hidden, the antonym of overt, public activity.

clue.text: Combined centres in almost accidental way

indicators.note: the centres of the next two words are taken and joined together

parts.note: the middle two letters of the six-letter word
the middle two letters of the ten-letter word

explanation.surface: Two things came together, almost by accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' looks like a deletion signal, but here it is a word whose middle letters are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: A mode is a manner or method of doing something, as in mode of transport.

clue.text: Like some music that, with initial repetitions, may be adapted for harpsichord

indicators.note: adapted means rearranged, so the instrument's letters are reordered
the answer's opening two letters, repeated, are the extra letters the keyboard name has beyond it

parts.note: the instrument, eleven letters
the answer's first two letters said again; removed from the instrument here to show the working

explanation.surface: Some music could be arranged to be played on a harpsichord.
explanation.walkthrough: Written in reverse: take the answer, repeat its first two letters R and H, and you can rearrange the result into HARPSICHORD.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhapsodic music is free, effusive and emotional in form, in the manner of a rhapsody.

clue.text: Intimate location for marriage announced, say, with love

indicators.note: announced means spoken out, so the place for marriage counts by its sound

parts.note: couples marry at the altar of a church
e.g., for example, means say
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A cosy wedding venue is announced, full of romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intimate' is the noun, a close friend, not the adjective the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: An alter ego can mean a very close and trusted friend, almost a second self.

clue.text: Classify as invalid after I had turned unhealthy-looking

indicators.note: turned means turned round, so the short form of 'I had' is read backwards

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had
a sallow face is a pale, yellowish, unhealthy colour

explanation.surface: A referee declares something void after they had turned a sickly colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned' reads as 'became', linking to 'unhealthy-looking'; it actually reverses I'D.
explanation.definitionFit: To disallow a goal or claim is to rule it invalid or unacceptable, officially rejecting it.

clue.text: Holder of position replaced, reprocessed, reorganized

indicators.note: reorganized puts the letters of 'reprocessed' in a new arrangement

parts.note: anagram fodder, eleven letters

explanation.surface: A post-holder has been swapped out, recycled and restructured, like a company in upheaval.
explanation.walkthrough: Three 're-' words in a row: the first belongs to the definition, the second is fodder and the third is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A predecessor is the person who previously held a post before the current incumbent took over.

clue.text: Prodigal's faults we must change

indicators.note: the letters of 'faults we' must change places

parts.note: anagram fodder, eight letters

explanation.surface: A spendthrift admits his own failings and resolves to reform.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Prodigal is 'is': Prodigal is the definition, and 'must change' works on the next two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A prodigal person spends extravagantly and recklessly, squandering resources, which is being wasteful.

clue.text: Like top US deputy, having evil power in relation to housing

parts.note: vice is wickedness
P stands for power in physics
re means concerning, in relation to
residential means relating to housing; with RE it forms the word

explanation.surface: America's number two turns out to be a villain with a stake in property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In relation to housing' is best read as one phrase meaning residential; the RE of 'in relation to' is its start.
explanation.definitionFit: The US deputy head of state is the vice-president, and this adjective describes that office.

clue.text: Philosopher and noble talked intermittently

parts.note: aristo is short for aristocrat, a noble

indicators.note: intermittently means on and off, so every other letter of 'talked' is kept

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: A philosopher and an aristocrat chatted now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noble' is a noun here, an aristocrat, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek thinker who tutored Alexander the Great is the most famous of all philosophers.

clue.text: In backward class, join top performers

indicators.note: going in backward order, the words for class and join are written from the end

parts.note: a class is a kind or sort
a seam is where two pieces are joined

explanation.surface: A pupil in a remedial class is invited to join the elite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backward class' looks like a slow stream at school; the whole run of two nouns is reversed together.
explanation.definitionFit: Maestros are masters of an art, especially eminent musicians and conductors at the top.

clue.text: Family with daughter, good-natured sort

parts.note: kin are one's family
d is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A household with a daughter who is a thoroughly nice person.
explanation.walkthrough: Two definitions sit together at the end: the adjective 'good-natured' and the noun 'sort'.
explanation.definitionFit: Kind as adjective means benevolent and considerate; as a noun it means type or variety.

clue.text: Moving cautiously after doctor, getting up from bed

indicators.note: after sends the words for moving cautiously second, behind the doctor's title

parts.note: Dr is the doctor's title
edging is moving slowly and carefully

explanation.surface: A patient creeps gingerly out of bed after the doctor's visit.
explanation.walkthrough: The bed is a river or sea bed, not a hospital bed: 'getting up' means bringing mud or objects up from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Dredging clears or scoops silt and material up from the floor of a harbour or river.

clue.text: Which person covering area gives order to stop?

parts.note: who asks which person
a is area; in a down clue the first piece covers it, sitting on top

explanation.surface: Who is responsible for this district, and who gives the order to halt?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Covering' is a positional word for a down clue: the first piece sits above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the command to a horse to halt, and more generally an instruction to slow down.

clue.text: Specialist knowing how to treat elders, for example

definitions.text: Specialist knowing how to treat elders, for example

parts.words: Specialist knowing how to treat elders
parts.note: surface: a geriatric doctor caring for older people
setter's reading: elders are also small trees with white flowers and black berries

explanation.surface: A doctor who specialises in caring for older people.
explanation.walkthrough: Elder is a shrub or small tree, whose flowers make elderflower cordial; the specialist looks after trees, not elderly patients.
explanation.definitionFit: This professional prunes, repairs and cares for trees, the arboriculture equivalent of a doctor.

clue.text: Part of our capital also hoarded, but only part

indicators.note: only part of the words 'also hoarded' is used, the run inside them

parts.note: the letters straddling the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: Someone stockpiled a share of the nation's wealth, though only some of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Our capital' is London, as The Times is a London paper; Soho is a district in its West End. 'Capital' looks like money.
explanation.definitionFit: Soho is a lively district of central London, famous for theatres, restaurants and nightlife.

clue.text: Doctor to charge NHS, be less than honest?

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters get rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder, eleven letters

explanation.surface: A physician billing the National Health Service could be a little dishonest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' is a verb, meaning falsify, not a physician. The NHS is Britain's free public health service.
explanation.definitionFit: To shortchange someone is to cheat them, giving less than is due, a mild dishonesty.

clue.text: Passed, having finished and understood

parts.note: when something is finished it is over
to take something in a certain way is to understand it

explanation.surface: A student passed the exam, having completed and grasped the material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passed' reads as succeeding in an exam; it means went past another vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A driver who overtook another car passed it, moving ahead on the road.

clue.text: As far as possible, coat flask ahead of time

indicators.note: ahead of places the flask before the letter for time

parts.note: an animal's coat is its fur
a Thermos is a vacuum flask
t is short for time

explanation.surface: Advice to insulate a flask as thoroughly as you can before the trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coat' is a noun, fur, not an instruction to cover something.
explanation.definitionFit: Furthermost means most distant or remote, lying at the greatest distance away.

clue.text: Repeated experience swallowing stimulant makes one carefree

indicators.note: the repeated experience swallows the drug, taking it inside

parts.note: to go through an experience again is to relive it
E is ecstasy, the stimulant drug

explanation.surface: Taking a pep pill over and over supposedly leaves you without worries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repeated experience' must be a past-tense verb, relived, for the letters to fit round the E.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone relieved has had anxiety lifted and feels untroubled, freed from worry.

clue.text: In ideal way, mother embracing two sons as leader of tributes

indicators.note: the phrase for ideally and the word for mother each embrace one of the two sons

parts.note: done to a T is done perfectly
s is son, twice
mater is Latin for mother, old public-school slang

explanation.surface: A mother, hugging her two boys perfectly, heads the round of speeches.
explanation.walkthrough: One son goes into each half: TO A (S) T, then MA (S) TER. 'To a T' means perfectly.
explanation.definitionFit: A toastmaster announces the speakers and proposes toasts at a formal dinner or banquet.

clue.text: Rapid succession of passes that may lead to scoring goal?

definitions.text: Rapid succession of passes that may lead to scoring goal?

parts.words: Rapid succession of passes that may lead to scoring goal?
parts.note: surface: a quick football move ending with the ball in the net
setter's reading: passes are romantic advances, and scoring is finding a partner

explanation.surface: A slick sequence of passes on the football pitch sets up a goal.
explanation.walkthrough: Every football word has a romantic second sense: passes are advances, scoring is pulling a partner, the goal a relationship.
explanation.definitionFit: At these events singles meet many potential partners in a series of brief timed conversations.

clue.text: His job allows him to overlook church

definitions.text: His job allows him to overlook church

parts.words: His job allows him to overlook church
parts.note: surface: someone whose work excuses him from attending services
setter's reading: to look down on the church from a great height

explanation.surface: A man's working hours give him an excuse to skip Sunday services.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overlook' means ignore in the surface but literally 'look over from above' in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This worker climbs tall towers and spires to repair them, gazing down on the building below.

clue.text: Record on one page how paper may be controlled

parts.note: a record is a disc
I is the Roman numeral one
p is short for page
paper is often lined, ruled for writing

explanation.surface: A note on a page about how a newspaper is managed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' just orders the pieces; 'how paper may be' is a descriptive phrase for a state of paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Disciplined behaviour is orderly and restrained, kept under strict self-command.

clue.text: As part of architectural essentials, what's more?

definitions.note: cryptic: in the motto 'less is more', this word is what is more

indicators.note: the answer forms part of the phrase 'architectural essentials', spanning its two words

parts.note: the last letter of the first word and first three of the second

explanation.surface: An architecture student asks what else belongs among the fundamentals.
explanation.walkthrough: Mies van der Rohe's modernist motto 'Less is more' makes the definition fair: in it, the answer is what 'is more'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the minimalist slogan of modern architecture, this word is equated with its opposite, more.

clue.text: Uniform officer put together for fellow sharing quarters

parts.note: uniform in the sense of even, level
a mate is an officer on a merchant ship

explanation.surface: A uniformed officer is assigned to share someone's lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uniform' is the adjective (level, even), not clothing and not the NATO letter U.
explanation.definitionFit: A flatmate is someone you share an apartment with, the British term for roommate.

clue.text: Highly-strung supporter of one kind of artist

definitions.text: Highly-strung supporter of one kind of artist

parts.words: Highly-strung supporter of one kind of artist
parts.note: surface: a nervous patron of the arts
setter's reading: literally strung up high, bearing a circus performer

explanation.surface: A nervy patron backs a particular sort of painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Highly-strung' means tense in the surface but literally strung high in the air; the artist is a circus walker.
explanation.definitionFit: A funambulist performs on this taut cable stretched high above the circus ring.

clue.text: One whose home is in a state, surrounded by water

definitions.text: One whose home is in a state, surrounded by water

parts.words: One whose home is in a state, surrounded by water
parts.note: surface: someone whose house is flooded and who is in a panic
setter's reading: an Australian state that is an island

explanation.surface: Someone's house is flooded and they are understandably agitated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a state' sounds like being upset; it is literally an Australian state, the one that is an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasmania is the island state south of mainland Australia, and this names a native or resident.

clue.text: Finding 17 or 51 in state becoming more mature

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly
aging is growing older

explanation.surface: Hunting for certain numbers in a nation that is growing older.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 across is MODE and 51 down is MEAN, both kinds of average, so finding either one is this.
explanation.definitionFit: The mode and the mean are statistical averages, so calculating one of them is this activity.

clue.text: World's response when Conservative rises to the top

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising to the top moves the party letter up from its place to the head of the column

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
REACTION, a response, with its C lifted out

explanation.surface: How the world reacts when a Tory politician climbs to power.
explanation.walkthrough: The C already sits in REACTION; it is moved from fourth place up to first. The 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Creation can mean the whole universe or world, everything that was brought into being.

clue.text: Without wife, at sixes and sevens? Not eating enough?

indicators.note: read in reverse, the answer without the wife letter leaves a phrase meaning sixes and sevens, so the letter must be inside

parts.note: sixes and sevens are numbers under eight
w is short for wife

explanation.surface: Without his wife he's all over the place, and not eating properly.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'at sixes and sevens' means in confusion, but here it is read literally as numbers under eight; the answer without W gives that phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who does not eat enough ends up weighing less than is healthy.

clue.text: Frank's father coming in immediately after time

indicators.note: the father's title comes in, entering the word for immediately after

parts.note: upon arrival means immediately after it
Fr is Father, a priest's title
t is short for time

explanation.surface: Frank's dad turns up straight after closing time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a name; it is the adjective meaning candid, and the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone upfront is open and candid about things, which is what frank means.

clue.text: Concert I watch as person entitled to expect something

parts.note: a Prom is one of the BBC Proms concerts in London
the letter as it stands
to watch is to see

explanation.surface: A concert-goer with a ticket feels entitled to a good performance.
explanation.walkthrough: The Proms are a famous summer season of BBC concerts; the legal term for the other party is the promisor.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, the promisee is the party to whom an undertaking is made, who may rely on it.

clue.text: Protest appearing in article, differently stressed
Pub count incomplete — one can hold many pints

indicators.note: incomplete means the word for count loses its last letter

parts.note: a bar is a pub
to count on someone is to rely on them; RELY cut short

explanation.surface: A pub's tally of drinks is unfinished, though one container holds plenty of beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Count' is the verb as in 'count on', meaning rely, not a tally.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrel is a large cask, and a beer barrel holds dozens of pints.

clue.text: Behind pool of money: let it be split, at last!

parts.note: a fund is a pool of money
amen means 'so be it'

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of 'split'

parts.note: the final letter of split

explanation.surface: Someone backs a money pool, hoping it will finally be divided up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' is the noun, the buttocks, not a preposition; 'be' belongs with 'let it', the literal sense of the prayer ending.
explanation.definitionFit: Fundament is a formal or humorous word for the buttocks, a person's bottom.

clue.text: One feature of skirt that attracts attention

parts.note: a means one
the folded, stitched lower edge of a skirt

explanation.surface: A detail of a skirt that turns heads.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a revealing skirt; the definition is the little cough used to get someone's notice.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the throat-clearing noise people make to draw notice or signal mild disapproval.

clue.text: Abraham Lincoln, initially, rebuilt palace

indicators.note: rebuilt means reconstructed, so the letters of the name are rearranged

parts.note: the first name as it stands

indicators.note: initially takes only the first letter of the surname Lincoln

parts.note: the opening letter of the surname

explanation.surface: The early President Lincoln restores a grand residence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' applies only to Lincoln; Abraham is used in full.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alhambra is the Moorish palace and fortress complex overlooking Granada in southern Spain.

clue.text: Represent base

explanation.walkthrough: 'Base' is the adjective, contemptible, not a foundation or military site.
explanation.definitionFit: Signs signify their meanings; separately, base conduct is petty and unworthy, which is mean.

clue.text: Starting point for big win, though lacking leaders

indicators.note: each of the three words loses its first letter, its leader

parts.note: without its F
without its B
without its W

explanation.surface: The beginning of a big victory, even though the team lacked its captains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' looks like a link word; it is the first of the three beheaded words.
explanation.definitionFit: An origin is where something begins, its source or beginning.

clue.text: Important IT role is new for teenager given new order

indicators.note: a new order is a fresh arrangement of the letters

parts.note: anagram fodder, sixteen letters

explanation.surface: A teenager takes on a big tech job for the first time.
